caveats: marginal_likelihood: the variance prior is fitted by mzLib's own maximum marginal likelihood, each feature's own residual df in the likelihood (VariancePriorEstimator.MarginalLikelihood). It is not limma's estimator (fitFDistUnequalDF1), so its numbers differ from default limma's; mzLib compares them with limma's, it does not require them equal. mzLib searches the prior df from about 0.05 (e^-3) upward, so a prior df there is that floor, not an optimum. Not implemented: robust = TRUE, the B-statistic, observation weights.
bh_adjusted is Benjamini-Hochberg over the fitted features, per coefficient and per contrast. It is not a target-decoy q-value.
Missing cells are omitted per feature, never imputed. A 0 is an observation: log-transform first, or blank out unmeasured values.

residual_df_differ: the fitted features do not all have the same residual degrees of freedom (missing values were omitted). marginal_likelihood handles that exactly, each feature's own df in the likelihood. Default limma (3.61 and later, eBayes legacy = FALSE) uses its own estimator for this case, so it would still report somewhat different numbers.
280 of 492 features were not fitted (214 too_few_observations, 66 rank_deficient); their statistics are null and they are not in the BH family.
15 response cells are exactly 0 and were fitted as observations. If 0 means 'not measured' in your table, blank those cells.
